description: What a person *is*, declared once so that a species is a value rather than a typo waiting to happen. The companion to cultures.json: that says what a person belongs to, this says what they are. Only characters carry `species` -- fauna and flora say what they are through `clade` and `base_species`, which is a different question with a different answer.
note: Four of these come in near-identical pairs -- asura/asura_tainted, vanara/vanara_spirit -- and they are deliberately not merged. Declaring the vocabulary is about catching the thirteenth value someone types by accident, not about flattening twelve real distinctions into eight. If a pair should collapse, that is an authoring decision made on the characters, not a lint rule.

species.note: Sentient and person-like rather than beast -- metal humans who behave as people do. The culture of the same name is `maya_born` in cultures.json; the creature sense is a base_species pairing in fauna. Three senses, three homes.
A god wearing a person, which is not the same as a god.
Touched by asura rather than being one. Kept distinct from `asura` on purpose: the taint is what the story turns on, and collapsing the two would lose it.
Neither wholly alive nor wholly spirit.
Human crossed with something canon has not named.
The first people of the Narmada, descended from the Narmada Man. A species, never a culture -- a draft proposed it as one and was refused.
The simian people of the Prehistoric era.
A vanara that is no longer only a vanara. Kept distinct from `vanara` for the same reason as the asura pair.
